content:
Looking to use Signal on multiple devices simultaneously? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to an existing Signal account, no longer limited to using an iPad as the second mobile device.

In addition to announcing Android linking capabilities today, the company stated: "We are expanding linked device support on iOS — beyond the iPad we've always supported, you can now link an iPhone to your Signal account."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their full message history, along with media files stored within the past 45 days.

Signal stated that the transfer process uses complete end-to-end encryption and employs the same "link-and-sync" technology used by iPad and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac).

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who need two iPhones to separate work and personal matters, or for those who need to test multiple devices.

This move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to the Apple Messages ecosystem, allowing users to seamlessly continue conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal version 8.22 for iOS is coming soon to the App Store. Signal has recently also introduced a username feature, allowing users to establish connections without sharing a phone number.
